Type.evidence_source: [/page/2/Text/6] An ethical clearance for conducting the study was obtained from the National Scientific Committee (VSN-17-087). Researchers set strict requirements for informed consent, that is that participants agreed voluntarily, knowing what they were consenting to. It was explained, both in a written form and orally, what the study was about, and it was clearly stated that participation could be cancelled at any time.

Area.evidence_source: [/page/2/Text/7] All the participants said participating in the study was a relief for them. They felt it was good to be able to disclose their difficult experience where they were uninterrupted and could just tell their story. This said, they related that at the time of the interviews they experienced some strain and stress but afterwards they experienced relief and had greater well-being. They related this in the second interview. Since there [/page/4/Text/5] was absolute anonymity in the study and no one knew the participants' identity except the first author, the men said that they experienced neither shame nor prejudice, which they related having been afraid of before the interviews.
